name: Meiga, Vedoira
body:
Vedoira
CR 4

This slender, dark-haired female humanoid has an aged wisdom in her eyes that belies her ageless face. Jeweled ornaments spangle her vestments.

XP 1,200
N Medium fey (extraplanar)
Init +4; Senses darkvision 60 ft., low-light vision; Perception +11

DEFENSE

AC 17, touch 15, flat-footed 12 (+4 Dex, +1 dodge, +2 natural)
hp 39 (6d6+18)
Fort +5, Ref +9, Will +7
DR 5/cold iron; Immune mind-affecting, sleep; SR 15

OFFENSE

Speed 30 ft.
Melee mwk dagger +8 (1d4/19–20 plus 2d8 force)
Special Attacks haunting curse
Spell-Like Abilities (CL 6th; concentration +9)

At will—chill touch (DC 14)
3/day—ray of enfeeblement (DC 14), sleep (DC 14)
1/day—dream, speak with dead (DC 16)

STATISTICS

Str 10, Dex 18, Con 17, Int 12, Wis 15, Cha 17
Base Atk +3; CMB +3; CMD 18
Feats Combat Casting, Dodge, Weapon Finesse
Skills Diplomacy +12, Intimidate +9, Knowledge (religion) +7, Perception +11, Sense Motive +11, Sleight of Hand +13, Stealth +13
Languages Common, Sylvan; telepathy 30 ft.
Gear mwk dagger

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Haunting Curse (Su)

As an immediate action when a creature within 120 feet of a vedoira makes an attack against her, she can unleash a vexing spirit to haunt her attacker. The target must succeed at a DC 16 Will save to avoid the spirit attaching itself to the target. The spirit can’t physically harm the target, but it can scream, whisper, threaten, or nudge or jostle the target.

The target has a –2 penalty on attack rolls and Strength– and Dexterity-based checks. When the target sleeps, it must succeed at a DC 16 Fort save or it only regains half the hit points from resting and is fatigued for the day. The vedoira can take a standard action to dismiss the spirit. Otherwise, remove curse banishes the spirit. This is a curse effect. The save DCs are Charisma-based.

ECOLOGY

Environment any land
Organization solitary, pair, or troupe (3-6)
Treasure standard

Vedoiras deal with dreams in which mortals are contacted by the spirits of the deceased. They are spirit mediums, able to guide spirits to the mortals they wish to contact and facilitate their communications. As such, the spirits of the dead hold these meiga in high esteem, and are quick to assist a vedoira against assailants, doing whatever is in their power to thwart her attackers. A vedoira appears as a young, slender woman wearing a flowing, colorful gown that flutters in an unfelt breeze. Faint whispers fill the air around her.
